Nimbus Home Goods -- Returns & Exchanges Policy (Section 4, revised March 2026)

4.1 General window: Items may be returned within 30 days of the delivery date for a full
refund to the original payment method, provided the item is unused.
4.2 Opened small-kitchen appliances (blenders, toasters, kettles, coffee makers): a 15%
restocking fee applies if the unit has been used, UNLESS the return is due to a manufacturer
defect, in which case the restocking fee is waived.
4.3 Clearance / Final Sale items (identified by a red "Clearance" tag at checkout) are not
eligible for return or exchange for any reason related to buyer's remorse, sizing, or change
of mind.
4.4 Exception overriding 4.3: a Clearance item may still be returned for a full refund if the
customer reports a manufacturer defect within 90 days of the delivery date. This exception
takes priority over the Clearance exclusion and is not subject to the 30-day general window
in 4.1.
4.5 Proof of purchase (order number or receipt) is required for all claims under this section.

---

Support ticket #58822
Submitted by: Priya Chandrasekaran
Order: #NHG-77410 (blender, "Vortex 500", Clearance tag applied at checkout)
Delivered: August 3, 2026
Ticket opened: September 20, 2026

Message from customer:
"Hi, I bought the Vortex 500 blender during your clearance sale back in early August. I know
it said final sale on the receipt, and I don't have a problem with that normally, but the
motor started smelling like burning plastic yesterday and now it won't turn on past speed 1.
I only used it maybe a dozen times to make smoothies, nothing crazy. I still have my order
confirmation email with the order number above. I don't want store credit, I'd like my money
back on the card I used since this is clearly not a case of me just changing my mind about it.
Let me know what you need from me."

Internal agent note (Devon, support tier 1): "Checked order #NHG-77410 in the system, delivery
confirmed 8/3. Item was flagged Clearance at time of sale, subtotal $34.99. No prior claims on
this order. Customer's description is consistent with a motor burnout, not water damage or
physical damage. Escalating per section 4.4 since this looks like a straightforward defect
claim within the 90-day defect window, not a remorse return."

Follow-up reply from Devon to customer, September 20, 2026, 4:10 PM:
"Hi Priya, thanks for the details and for holding onto your order confirmation. I want to set
expectations clearly since I know Clearance items usually can't be returned. Section 4.3 of
our policy does exclude Clearance purchases from returns for reasons like sizing or change of
mind. However, section 4.4 carves out a specific exception: if a Clearance item develops a
manufacturer defect and you report it within 90 days of delivery, that exception takes
priority over the Clearance exclusion, and it isn't limited by the normal 30-day window
either. Based on your description -- a burning smell and the motor cutting out after normal
use, not anything that sounds like misuse or damage -- this reads as a defect claim to me.

Before I finalize anything, can you confirm two things: (1) that you still have the order
confirmation email handy in case our records ever need a second reference, and (2) that the
blender hasn't been dropped, exposed to liquid beyond normal cleaning, or modified in any way?
I ask only because those would change how we classify the claim. Assuming the answers are what
I expect based on your message, I'll process this as a full refund to your original payment
method rather than store credit, since the defect exception restores your normal 4.1 refund
terms."

Customer reply, September 20, 2026, 4:45 PM:
"Yes, I still have the confirmation email, and no, I never dropped it or got it wet -- it lived
on my kitchen counter the whole time and I only ever used it for smoothies and the occasional
soup base. Thank you for explaining the sections, that makes sense. Please go ahead and
process the refund to my card whenever you're able to."

flight (a "no-show") forfeits all remaining segments on that itinerary. Exception: passengers
holding Platinum elite status have their remaining segments automatically protected instead
of forfeited.

Case: Passenger itinerary NW-6120, round trip. Passenger holds Platinum elite status and
missed the outbound flight without canceling or notifying the airline in advance. The return
flight is scheduled for 4 days later. Gate agent notes from the outbound departure: passenger
never checked in and did not respond to the final boarding call; no advance notice of a
schedule conflict was received by the airline through any channel (phone, app, or website)
before departure. The passenger's account shows Platinum status has been active for over a
year, well before this itinerary was booked.

questions.instruction: Are the passenger's remaining flight segments protected rather than forfeited?
questions.notes: Platinum status triggers automatic protection, overriding the general no-show forfeiture rule.

questions.instruction: What happens to the return flight segment on itinerary NW-6120?

candidates.description: It is automatically protected because of Platinum status
It is forfeited under the standard no-show policy
It is rebooked onto a different route for a fee
It is refunded to the original payment method

questions.notes: Platinum status is the specific, stated exception to the general forfeiture rule.

state:
TerraTech Appliances warranty policy: covered repairs are free (parts and labor) for 12
months from the purchase date. If a covered repair's estimated cost exceeds 50% of the item's
current retail value, TerraTech replaces the unit with a refurbished equivalent instead of
repairing it.

Repair ticket: Blender purchased 6 months ago for $120 (original price). Current retail value
of this model: $100. Technician's repair estimate: $65 for a new motor assembly. Issue
confirmed as a manufacturer defect, not misuse. Technician notes: "Motor housing shows no
signs of drops or liquid intrusion; failure pattern matches a known bearing defect in this
production batch. Customer has been cooperative and provided the original purchase receipt
showing the date and price. Recommending we proceed under warranty rather than treating this
as a billable repair."

questions.instruction: Is the blender still within its 12-month manufacturer warranty period?
questions.notes: 6 months have passed, which is within the 12-month coverage period.

questions.instruction: Does the repair estimate exceed the 50%-of-current-value replacement threshold?
questions.notes: $65 is 65% of the $100 current retail value, above the 50% threshold.

questions.instruction: What resolution applies under warranty?

candidates.description: Repair the unit using the $65 estimate
Replace the unit with a refurbished equivalent
Deny the claim as out of warranty
Bill the customer the full repair cost

questions.notes: In-warranty and the $65 estimate exceeds 50% of the $100 current value, so it is replaced, not repaired.

state:
Voltix Electronics -- Warranty Terms

Section 2: Standard hardware warranty runs 24 months from the purchase date, PROVIDED the
product was registered online within 30 days of purchase. Products that are not registered
within that window default to a shortened 90-day warranty from the purchase date. Water
damage and cosmetic wear are excluded from coverage under all circumstances, registered or
not.

---

Support ticket #71190
Product: Voltix PowerBook charging port
Purchased: January 10, 2026
Ticket opened: September 12, 2026 (device is roughly 8 months old)

Customer message: "My PowerBook has completely stopped charging. It just won't take a charge
from any cable or adapter I try, and there's no visible damage to the port that I can see.
I bought it in January and I'd like this fixed or replaced under warranty. I don't have any
other issues to report -- battery life was fine until this happened suddenly two days ago."

Agent reply (Kayla, support tier 1), September 12, 2026, 3:30 PM: "Thanks for the details.
Sorry to hear about the charging issue -- a sudden total failure with no visible port damage
does sound consistent with an internal fault rather than something like a bent pin from cable
misuse, so I don't think we'd need to worry about a damage exclusion here. Before I can tell
you which warranty term applies to your PowerBook, I need to check whether it was registered.
Could you let me know if you completed the online registration step when you first set up the
device back in January? I don't see a registration record pulled up automatically on my end,
but sometimes those take a moment to sync, so I wanted to ask you directly rather than assume."

Customer reply, September 12, 2026, 5:05 PM: "Hi Kayla, honestly I'm not sure -- I set this up
for my dad and he does most of his own tech stuff, so I don't know if he went through a
registration step or not. He's traveling right now and hard to reach today. Is there anything
else you can check on your end in the meantime? I'd really like to get this sorted since he
needs the laptop for work calls."

Agent reply (Kayla), September 12, 2026, 5:40 PM: "Understood, no problem. I checked our
registration database again using the serial number on file and the order number from
January, and I'm still not finding any registration record tied to this unit as of today. I'll
note the account and proceed based on what's confirmed in our system rather than wait
indefinitely, since we don't have anyone available right now who can confirm the registration
step was completed. I'll follow up once I've determined which warranty term applies and what
the next steps are for getting the charging issue resolved."

[No registration confirmation, registration date, or mention of a completed online
registration step appears anywhere else in the ticket, account notes, or attached files.]

questions.instruction: Was this PowerBook registered online within 30 days of purchase?
questions.notes: Nothing in the ticket confirms registration; absence of evidence means the answer is no.

questions.instruction: What warranty term applies to this device?

candidates.description: 24 months, because it was registered on time
90 days, the default for unregistered products
12 months, a flat standard term
No warranty is available for this product line

questions.notes: With no registration evidence, the shortened 90-day default term applies.

questions.instruction: Is the device still within its warranty period as of the ticket date?
questions.notes: 8 months exceeds the 90-day unregistered term (about 3 months).

state:
Halcyon Mobile coverage rules: the Care+ extended plan covers accidental damage, up to 2
claims per rolling 12-month period, with a $49 deductible per claim. Manufacturer defects are
covered at no charge under the standard warranty regardless of Care+ enrollment. When a
single repair involves BOTH an accidental-damage issue and an unrelated manufacturer defect,
only the defect portion is free; the accidental-damage portion is still billed at the Care+
deductible.

Technician report: Customer's phone has a cracked screen (customer confirms they dropped the
phone) and, separately, a swelling battery that the technician identifies as an unrelated
manufacturer defect. Customer is enrolled in Care+ and has filed zero claims in the past 12
months.

questions.instruction: Will the customer be charged anything for this repair?
questions.notes: The cracked screen is accidental damage, billed at the $49 Care+ deductible.

questions.instruction: Which repairs are covered at no charge under the standard warranty?

candidates.description: The cracked screen repair
The battery replacement

questions.notes: Only the unrelated manufacturer defect (battery) is free; the drop damage is not.

questions.instruction: How much will the customer be billed in total for this repair visit?

candidates.description: The full retail repair cost for both issues

questions.notes: Only the single Care+ deductible applies to the accidental-damage portion.

Ferrotech Tablets policy: devices reported dead-on-arrival (DOA) within 14 days of delivery
are replaced with a new unit at no charge, with no repair attempt required. After 14 days,
standard warranty repair procedures apply instead.

Case: customer's tablet, delivered 10 days ago, will not power on at all under any
circumstances (tried multiple outlets and cables).

questions.instruction: Does the DOA replacement policy apply to this tablet?
questions.notes: 10 days since delivery is within the 14-day DOA window.

questions.instruction: What resolution applies to this case?

candidates.description: Free replacement with a new unit, no repair attempt
Standard warranty repair process
Denied because the DOA window has passed
A billable diagnostic and repair

questions.notes: Within the 14-day DOA window, so a repair attempt is not required.

questions.instruction: Which of the following exceptions or fees apply to this DOA claim?

candidates.description: A restocking fee applies

Purchase of an extended warranty is required

questions.notes: A clean within-window DOA claim carries none of these fees or requirements.

state:
Aurelia Corp warranty policy: the manufacturer warranty applies only to units purchased new
directly from Aurelia Corp or from a retailer on Aurelia's published list of authorized
resellers, and only with valid proof of purchase. Units purchased through unauthorized
third-party sellers -- including most online marketplace and auction listings -- are not
covered, regardless of the unit's age, condition, or the nature of the problem.

Case: Customer bought an Aurelia laptop 3 months ago from an individual seller on a general
online marketplace, not from the official Aurelia store or any retailer on Aurelia's
authorized list. The customer has the original receipt from that marketplace transaction. The
laptop now has a confirmed hardware defect (keyboard controller failure).

questions.instruction: Is this laptop covered under Aurelia's manufacturer warranty?
questions.notes: Purchase from an unauthorized marketplace seller voids coverage, despite the receipt and confirmed defect.

questions.instruction: Why is this warranty claim denied?

candidates.description: The claim is outside the warranty time period
The unit was purchased from an unauthorized third-party seller
No proof of purchase was provided
The type of damage is not a covered category

questions.notes: The seller's authorization status is the disqualifying factor, not time, proof, or damage type.

questions.instruction: Which of the following are true about this purchase and claim?

candidates.description: The purchase is within the warranty's normal time window
The seller is an authorized Aurelia reseller
The customer provided proof of purchase
A hardware defect was confirmed

questions.notes: Three conditions are met, but the unauthorized-seller exclusion still voids coverage.
